claims.text: The starting catalyst is a nearly equiatomic Co-Ni-Fe-Cr high-entropy alloy containing only a minor amount of Pd.
A short oxidative treatment at 300–350°C for approximately 30 minutes in O2, about 5% H2O, and trace NO can produce the proposed beneficial surface state.
Fine-tuning treatment temperature, duration, and gas composition can prevent over-oxidation and control oxide-overlayer thickness.
The oxidative treatment forms a self-limiting multi-element oxide overlayer.
The oxide overlayer becomes enriched in redox-active elements, especially Cr, through selective surface segregation.
A trace oxygen-active dopant such as Ce could also become enriched in the oxide overlayer if present.
The oxide layer acts as a protective barrier against sintering and thermal degradation.
The oxide layer modulates active sites to promote NO oxidation or reduction.
The oxide layer promotes hydrocarbon activation without excessively obstructing active sites.
Excessive oxide-layer growth can block active sites and reduce catalytic activity.
The treated catalyst will have higher low-temperature catalytic activity than the untreated catalyst.
The treated catalyst will retain performance better during extended mileage and thermal aging than the untreated catalyst.
The oxidative treatment will preserve low platinum-group-metal usage.
The untreated catalyst suffers activity loss and durability limitations under transient low-temperature exhaust, particularly with H2O, NO, and thermal aging.
The proposed treatment is expected to work under transient exhaust conditions of 300–350°C, about 5% H2O, and trace NO.
The proposed benefit is not expected to extend to high-temperature regimes or substantially different exhaust environments.

contradictions.description: Reduced activity after intentional over-oxidation is presented as an expected consequence of excessive active-site blocking, but the falsification rule also treats that same expected result as sufficient to refute the hypothesis. It therefore does not cleanly distinguish confirmation of the proposed thickness dependence from falsification.
